patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact top navigation bar with a small menu icon/button at the far right, implying a collapsed navigation that must open and close on tap.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should reveal and hide the mobile navigation panel/list. The button should reflect expanded/collapsed state and likely swap icon state when open.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a dropdown below the header, an overlay, or a slide-out panel.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch includes a horizontal navigation row beneath the large hero/header area with multiple top-level items, which strongly implies at least one expandable submenu in desktop navigation. The reference layout also supports category-style nested navigation.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A top-level nav item may reveal a submenu on hover or click. If implemented, submenu visibility and active state should be synchronized for mouse and keyboard users.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch itself does not explicitly draw the submenu open state, so the exact trigger model (hover vs click) is not certain.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include a rectangular search field in the sidebar/lower content area, indicating a searchable site section with user text entry and submission behavior.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: The field should accept input and submit a search query, likely via Enter key or adjacent submit control. JS may enhance focus handling, clear state, or live submission behavior.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not indicate whether results are live/autocomplete or only submitted traditionally.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The sidebar sections, especially the category-like stacked lists with headings and nested items, imply expandable/collapsible groups rather than permanently open content. This is especially likely on mobile where vertical space is constrained.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Section headers or toggle controls should expand/collapse nested lists or content blocks. State should be conveyed visually and via ARIA-expanded semantics.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether all sidebar boxes are collapsible or only hierarchical category groups.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a long vertical sequence of repeated product/image cards continuing down the page, suggesting progressive disclosure or additional content retrieval as users browse deeper.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A load-more trigger could append more product cards after the initial set, especially on mobile to reduce initial payload. If used, loading state should be announced and focus/order preserved.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch could also represent a fully server-rendered long list with no JS loading at all; no explicit button is drawn.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply relatively light-to-moderate JavaScript overall: mobile needs the clearest explicit interaction via a hamburger-controlled navigation, while both viewports likely need search behavior and some collapsible sidebar/category treatment. Desktop appears more navigation-heavy with a probable dropdown in the horizontal nav, whereas mobile emphasizes stacked browsing through repeated cards and may benefit from progressive loading, though that part is speculative from the sketch alone.
